_: LP-854 review, round two - the SHARED corpus for the href rule.
two languages, and a rule written twice is two rules until something says otherwise. Both
test suites read THIS file and assert their own implementation gives the answer below, so a
change to either side that moves the rule fails on both.
WHY A CORPUS AND NOT A COMPARISON. The two were checked by running 24 hrefs through both
and found to agree - which was true, and did not mean they implemented the same rule. Four
more cases separated them, all in the direction where the EDITOR says safe and the
SANITISER says no: an editor accepting a link the server then strips, which is a link
vanishing on save. They are listed under `refused` and marked below.
THE RULE IS WHATWG's: strip leading and trailing C0 controls and space, remove tab, CR and
LF anywhere, lowercase, then compare the scheme. Nothing else is removed - a zero-width
space, a non-breaking space and a BOM all stay, because no browser removes them either, and
a rule that did would call h<ZWSP>ttp://x.com safe and store a link to nowhere.
